name: DroidFinestra
author: hamed7ir
description: DroidFinestra is a Windows GUI for scrcpy that mirrors and controls an Android phone over USB or Wi-Fi. It keeps per-device profiles with presets such as "Surface RT — balanced", builds the scrcpy command line from the chosen profile, pairs phones over Wi-Fi and shows scrcpy's live output. This package carries scrcpy, adb and FFmpeg built for 32-bit ARM Windows (scrcpy-rt, adb-rt, ffmpeg-rt) and runs on Windows RT 8.0 and 8.1 and Windows 10 ARM32, needing only the .NET Framework 4.0 that Windows RT already includes. DroidFinestra launches scrcpy without modifying it; scrcpy is by Genymobile.
dependencies: .NET Framework 4.0 or later — built into Windows 8 and Windows RT
USB debugging enabled on the Android phone
instructionSteps: On Windows RT, jailbreak the device first — RT only runs unsigned desktop apps after the jailbreak.
Run the installer. It installs per user into %LocalAppData%\Programs\DroidFinestra and needs no administrator rights; it checks the requirements first and reports anything missing.
At the SmartScreen warning choose More info, then Run anyway — the files are not signed.
On the phone, enable USB debugging (Developer options), then connect it by USB and accept the USB-debugging prompt on the phone.
In DroidFinestra choose New profile, start from a preset, and press Launch. DroidFinestra shows the scrcpy command line, then scrcpy's live output.

For Wi-Fi: on the phone open Wireless debugging and choose Pair device with pairing code; in DroidFinestra open the menu, choose Pair a phone over Wi-Fi, and enter the pairing address and code, then the connect address. Addresses are typed, not discovered.
Keep --render-driver=direct3d on (every preset has it): without it the scrcpy window is black on Tegra 3 hardware such as the Surface RT.
